pages.text: The vintage tram: 40 km/h, nine seats, a controller at each end.

Two trams, made for $(l:track/street_track)street track$(/l) and $(l:electric/overhead_lines)overhead wires$(/l). Both run from the wire, with a small battery for junctions and gaps (or charge at a charging point), and ring a bell.$(br2)The $(l)Vintage Tram$() runs both ways: get in as the driver at the end you want to lead. Its trolley pole trails behind it to the wire.

The $(l)Low-Floor Tram$() is three sections that bend round corners, about fourteen blocks in all: click a track block with it to put all three on together, and breaking any of them takes the whole tram up. Drive it from either end: about 50 km/h, fourteen seats.
The low-floor tram round a street corner.

A tram stops a block or so short of anything on the track ahead, people, animals, cars or other trains, and waits for them to clear, ringing its bell; animals that won't move are nudged off after a few seconds. With Reiko's Car Mod it stops at red traffic lights beside the line that face it, too. It brakes harder than a train.
